what_its_for: This medicine is used to relieve symptoms of the common cold, flu, and allergies. Acetaminophen helps reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain such as headache, body aches, and sore throat. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that helps relieve runny nose, sneezing, watery eyes, and itching caused by allergies or a cold.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food. Swallow tablets or capsules whole with a full glass of water. If using a liquid form, use the measuring cup or spoon that comes with the package — do not use a regular kitchen spoon, as it may give you the wrong dose. Do not crush, chew, or break extended-release tablets. Take only as directed on the label or as told by your doctor or pharmacist.
dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older: the typical dose is 1 to 2 tablets or the recommended amount of liquid every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Do not take more than 4 doses in 24 hours. Do not take more than 4,000 mg of acetaminophen per day from all sources. For children under 12: always check the package label for the correct child dose based on your child's weight and age, or ask your doctor or pharmacist. Never guess a child's dose.
missed_dose: This medicine is usually taken only when you need it for symptom relief, so a strict dosing schedule may not apply. If you are taking it on a regular schedule and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Check the expiration date on the package and safely dispose of any unused or expired medicine — do not flush down the toilet unless the label says it is safe to do so.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Alcohol can increase your risk of liver damage from acetaminophen and can also make drowsiness from chlorpheniramine much worse. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause drowsiness or dizziness. Do not take any other medicines that contain acetaminophen at the same time, including other cold, flu, pain, or sleep medicines — this can lead to a dangerous overdose. Check all medicine labels carefully. Avoid taking this medicine with other antihistamines or sedatives unless your doctor says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you: take more than the recommended dose or think you may have overdosed (even if you feel fine, because liver damage from acetaminophen may not show up right away); develop a skin rash, blistering, or peeling skin; have trouble breathing or swallowing; experience swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; have severe dizziness or confusion; notice your skin or eyes turning yellow (signs of liver problems); develop a high fever that does not go away; or if your symptoms do not improve after 7 days or get worse. Also call your doctor before taking this medicine if you have liver disease, kidney disease, glaucoma, enlarged prostate, a breathing condition like asthma or emphysema, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
when_it_works: You should start to feel relief from your symptoms within 30 minutes to 1 hour after taking this medicine. It usually works best for 4 to 6 hours. This medicine treats your symptoms but does not cure the underlying cold, flu, or allergy. If your symptoms do not improve within 7 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): You may be more sensitive to the drowsiness and dizziness caused by chlorpheniramine. Use caution when standing up quickly, as this medicine can increase your risk of falls. Your doctor may recommend a lower dose. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine. Chlorpheniramine may pass into breast milk and could affect a nursing baby. Children: Always use the dose recommended for your child's age and weight. Do not give adult formulations to children unless directed by a doctor. Liver or kidney problems: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine, as acetaminophen is processed by the liver and may need dose adjustments or may not be safe for you.
